eyebrow: The pricing shape, not exact figures
code:
# Both Azure and AWS, same basic shape:
#   data transfer INTO the cloud  -> typically free
#   data transfer OUT of the cloud -> metered, billed per GB
#
# From AWS's point of view, Azure is just an external network.
# A response AWS sends back to Azure is AWS egress — billed
# on AWS's side, regardless of how the link was built.
caption: The direction data flows has real cost consequences — this is an asymmetric cost, not a symmetric one.

eyebrow: What the asymmetry pushes you toward

steps.label: Minimize cross-cloud round trips per request
steps.sub: a chatty fetch-enrich-write-back pattern pays egress on every leg

steps.label: Batch instead of calling repeatedly
steps.sub: fewer, larger transfers beat many small ones

steps.label: Cache locally in the calling cloud
steps.sub: instead of re-fetching cross-cloud on every request

subtitle: One cloud degrading doesn't mean the other one did too — if the design accounts for that.
